title: Anthropic Posts First Profitable Quarter as Revenue Doubles to $10.9 Billion
excerpt: The AI startup's Q2 performance, driven by surging enterprise demand for Claude, puts it in direct competition with OpenAI ahead of dueling IPO timelines.
body:
• Anthropic projects $10.9 billion in Q2 2026 revenue, more than doubling the $4.8 billion posted in Q1, with a $559 million operating profit marking its first profitable quarter.
  • The company is in talks to raise fresh capital at a valuation exceeding $900 billion, surpassing OpenAI's most recent $852 billion private valuation.
  • Claude Code, Anthropic's AI coding assistant, has reached $2.5 billion in annualized revenue within six months of launch, with more than 1,000 enterprise clients spending over $1 million annually.
  • Both Anthropic and OpenAI are eyeing public offerings in late 2026, setting up the most consequential year for AI IPOs in history.

Anthropic has told investors it expects $10.9 billion in second-quarter revenue and $559 million in operating profit, which would mark the company's first profitable quarter since its founding in 2021. The figures, disclosed as part of an ongoing funding round, represent a 127% increase over the $4.8 billion recorded in Q1 — and exceed Anthropic's entire 2025 annual revenue in a single quarter.

From Safety-First Underdog to Enterprise Powerhouse

Founded by siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei after their departure from OpenAI, Anthropic built its reputation on safety-first AI development. That positioning has evolved into a commercial juggernaut. The company's annual revenue run rate topped $47 billion by May, up from $30 billion in April and roughly $9 billion at the end of 2025 — a trajectory that amounts to more than 10-fold annual growth in each of the past three years.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=XeXMUOigCaQ

The engine behind that growth is enterprise adoption of Claude's AI agent tools, particularly Claude Code. The coding assistant crossed $1 billion in revenue within six months of its launch and was running at $2.5 billion in annualized revenue by May 2026. Eight of the Fortune 10 are now Claude customers, and the number of clients spending more than $1 million annually doubled between April and May to surpass 1,000.

"Doubling revenue quarter-over-quarter to nearly $11 billion while hitting an operating profit milestone at a $900 billion valuation is not an underdog story — it is the story of a company that has emerged as OpenAI's most serious enterprise rival."

— Lumida News analysis

The IPO Race Takes Shape

Anthropic has confidentially filed for an IPO and is exploring a public offering as early as October, putting it on a potential collision course with OpenAI, which is targeting a September debut. The company is simultaneously negotiating a funding round at a valuation exceeding $900 billion — which would eclipse OpenAI's most recent private market valuation of $852 billion.

The profitability milestone, even if not sustained in future quarters, gives Anthropic a financial narrative that OpenAI currently cannot match. OpenAI has told investors it expects to reach profitability in 2030 after spending more than $600 billion on computing infrastructure. By contrast, Anthropic's operating margin of roughly 5% on Q2 revenue demonstrates that the unit economics of frontier AI can work — though the company has cautioned that margins will compress as it ramps spending on compute.

Anthropic has signed massive infrastructure deals, including a commitment to spend $15 billion annually on computing power from SpaceX, alongside longer-term agreements with Google and Amazon that could total hundreds of billions more.

What It Means for the AI Industry

Anthropic's results validate the strategic bet on AI agents. As businesses deploy autonomous AI systems to complete tasks rather than simply answer questions, the volume and value of compute consumed rises dramatically. The shift from chatbots to agents has created a new commercial category where Anthropic's Claude has emerged as a primary beneficiary.

For Indian-origin tech professionals across the Bay Area and beyond, the Anthropic-OpenAI rivalry has direct implications. Both companies are hiring aggressively, and the enterprise AI tools they build are reshaping software development workflows at companies where South Asian engineers hold significant leadership and engineering roles.

What's Next

The first mover in the public market will likely set the valuation benchmark for the other. Investor appetite for AI stocks remains strong, but it is not infinite. Anthropic's next frontier model release — the Mythos class, previewed in April — could further boost interest, particularly given the model's demonstrated ability to find high-severity security vulnerabilities in major operating systems and browsers.

Whether Anthropic can sustain its growth rate while managing ballooning compute costs will determine whether the company's near-trillion-dollar valuation holds up under public market scrutiny.
